title: KDASO: Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization for Liability Adjudication Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.06972v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Liability adjudication tasks (e.g., legal charge determination) require analyzing event descriptions against domain-specific skills to determine whether a party should bear liability. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in this area by leveraging executable skills for interpretable reasoning, existing approaches face three critical limitations: skill libraries become stale as real-world scenarios dynamically evolve, skill descriptions often suffer from a semantic execution gap where LLMs deviate from intended expert logic, and growing skill collections exceed context budgets causing critical skill omission. translated_title: KDASO：面向责任裁定任务的知识与数据双驱动自动技能优化
translated_abstract: 责任裁定任务（例如法律罪名认定）需要基于领域特定技能分析事件描述，以判断当事人是否应当承担责任。尽管大型语言模型（LLM）通过利用可执行技能实现可解释推理，在这一领域展现出潜力，但现有方法面临三个关键局限：随着真实世界场景的动态演变，技能库会逐渐过时；技能描述常存在语义执行鸿沟，导致LLM偏离预期的专家逻辑；不断增长的技能集合超出上下文预算，造成关键技能被遗漏。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了知识与数据双驱动的自动技能优化框架（KDASO），通过基于邻域条件从最新裁定数据中进行归纳、基于LLM执行轨迹分析进行执行对齐的技能优化、以及上下文预算路由等方式，持续演化技能库……
tldr: KDASO提出了一种知识与数据双驱动的自动技能优化框架，通过从最新裁定数据归纳新技能、基于执行轨迹对齐优化技能描述以及上下文预算路由，解决了LLM在责任裁定任务中技能库过时、语义执行鸿沟和关键技能遗漏三大问题。
en_tdlr: KDASO proposes a knowledge-data dual-driven automated skill optimization framework that tackles stale skill libraries, semantic execution gaps, and critical skill omission in LLM-based liability adjudication through neighborhood-conditioned induction from recent adjudication data, execution-aligned refinement, and context-budgeted skill routing.
